evidence: Hor. C. 3.1.47–48: cūr valle permūtem Sabīnā dīvitiās operōsiōrēs?
terms.comment: One of the two things goes in the ablative; the context shows which is given and which received (Lewis & Short s.v. mūtō).

evidence: Sall. J. 18.9: mūtāre rēs inter sē īnstituerant
terms.comment: Its everyday sense is “change”; of goods, to barter (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: cūr valle permūtem Sabīnā dīvitiās operōsiōrēs?
phrases.english: why should I trade my Sabine valley for riches that are more trouble?

phrases.latin: sub noctem quī puer ūvam furtīvā mūtat strigilī
phrases.english: the slave boy who at nightfall swaps a stolen strigil for a bunch of grapes

sources: Lewis & Short: permuto · Lewis & Short: muto
